title: FG House / Oficina Conceito Arquitetura
text:
FG House / Oficina Conceito Arquitetura

Located in the southern zone of Porto Alegre, Casa FG was conceived as an urban refuge: a contemporary residence that embraces the site's 16-foot slope as a design concept, making the view of the Guaíba River the central focus. The property, previously occupied by a house that felt more like a country estate, retains a close-knit neighborhood character typical of smaller towns — a rare and valuable quality in an urban context. It was here that the family found the perfect spot for their new home, featuring a spacious social area, bedrooms, a swimming pool, a terrace, and a pool house.

text:
Casa Canal / Este Norte Estudio

Yes, you are tucked away in the middle of the woods, and sometimes I think I can't see you from above because the treetops hide you. So I look for your left side, the one touching the river, and there I find you. Sometimes I look at you from the front and I can't believe how you turned out, because we designed you to be fresh and, truth be told, you are. And I'm not sure if that is so easily achieved.

text:
House in Santa Maria da Feira / Branco-DelRio Arquitectos

The house is situated on a walled, densely wooded plot, where the presence of mature vegetation defines the character of the site and establishes a sense of interiority and privacy. The property is set on sloping terrain organized around a courtyard, whose spatial structure and relationship with the topography were preserved as the foundation of the project.

title: Indigenous House / Formline Architecture + Urbanism + LGA Architectural Partners
text:
Indigenous House / Formline Architecture + Urbanism + LGA Architectural Partners

Indigenous House reflects the University of Toronto Scarborough's commitment to renewing and strengthening its relationship with Indigenous communities. Prominently situated at the centre of campus, the project plays a meaningful and visible role in the university's academic and cultural mission to address Canada's Truth and Reconciliation Commission's Calls to Action.

title: MacIsaac Health Building / SHL
text:
MacIsaac Health Building / SHL

The University of British Columbia (UBC) in Vancouver, Canada, ranks among the world's best universities. The new MacIsaac Health Building at the university's Point Grey campus entrance is designed to reflect UBC's reputation as a world-class institution for higher education, as well as its promise to support inclusivity, sustainability, and student well-being.

title: Call for Submissions: Figures of Architecture
text:
Call for Submissions: Figures of Architecture

Architecture is often understood through finished buildings. “Figures of Architecture” asks students to look closer at the things that make architecture possible: the materials, assemblies, and methods that are often concealed, overlooked, or misunderstood once a building is complete.

The competition challenges students to bring these typically unseen “Figures of Architecture” into focus and reconsider their role through the lens of climate resilience and adaptation.

Propose a design-build, or make one still image. Both streams are judged and awarded separately; three Built finalists then build their proposals. All winning projects will be exhibited at DesignTO Festival 2027.

title: Performing Colonial Toxicity

Performing Colonial Toxicity

From 24 October to 1 November 2026, Aguas Internacionales, located in the En Corts neighbourhood of Valencia, will host the international exhibition Performing Colonial Toxicity by historian and researcher Samia Henni.

The exhibition Performing Colonial Toxicity explores what Samia Henni describes as colonial toxicity, referring to French counterinsurgency operations in Algiers and nuclear testing in the Sahara Desert. title: The Mangrove as a Wall: Coastal Protection and Urban Development in India
text:
The Mangrove as a Wall: Coastal Protection and Urban Development in India

Along India's coast, the boundary between land and sea is not always a line of concrete. In places, it is a forest of tangled roots, tidal channels, and sediment, a landscape that changes character with the water. Mangroves influence how water moves, how shorelines evolve, and how coastal communities experience flood risk. Their role in coastal protection depends on the width and condition of the forest, the movement of tides, and the accumulation of sediment.

title: DUA Villa / Architecture BRIO
text:
DUA Villa / Architecture BRIO

DUA Villa is a weekend residence located in Alibaug, designed for a Mumbai-based couple and their three young adult children. As urban dwellers accustomed to the pace and density of city life, they sought a retreat offering proximity to nature without being overwhelmed by it.

title: From Paper to Space: Matter as Sensory Architecture
text:
From Paper to Space: Matter as Sensory Architecture

Selecting a material during the design process involves more than defining an appearance. Its behavior in response to light, sound, touch, and the passage of time can transform how a space is perceived and used. At the same time, factors such as durability, strength, recyclability, and the environmental impact associated with its production introduce new variables into architectural decision-making. For Stephanie Forsythe and Todd MacAllen, cofounders of Vancouver-based design and production studio molo, these considerations have led to an exploration of paper and its potential to shape flexible, sensory spaces.

title: Snøhetta’s Shanghai Grand Opera House Opens With a Sweeping Roof and Panoramic River Views
text:
Snøhetta’s Shanghai Grand Opera House Opens With a Sweeping Roof and Panoramic River Views

The Shanghai Grand Opera House, designed by Snøhetta in collaboration with East China Architectural Design & Research Institute (ECADI), Theatre Projects, and Nagata Acoustics, officially opened on October 17, 2026, along the Huangpu River in Shanghai, China. The opening marks the completion of a cultural project selected through an international design competition in 2016 and developed over the following decade. Located in the Expo Houtan district, the 146,786-square-meter building brings together three performance venues, production facilities, and publicly accessible spaces as part of the ongoing transformation of Shanghai's waterfront.

title: TOUR / GENS
text:
TOUR / GENS

An association dedicated to personal care is building its headquarters in an upscale residential suburb. Two needs are to be met: to allow flexibility in its layout for future evolution and to display the image of integrity, transparency, and a welcoming spirit.

title: Nakshabid Architects’ Alternative Factory Model in Bangladesh Receives the RIBA International Prize 2026
text:
Nakshabid Architects’ Alternative Factory Model in Bangladesh Receives the RIBA International Prize 2026

The Green Field Factory of Karupannya Rangpur Limited, designed by Nakshabid Architects, has been named the recipient of the RIBA International Prize 2026. Since 2016, the RIBA International Prize has been awarded to "a building that demonstrates visionary thinking, originality, excellence of execution, and makes a distinct contribution to its users, surrounding environment and communities." This year, the Green Field Factory was recognized for offering an alternative model for factory design and operation, challenging traditional workplace environments and creating new opportunities for women workers. The shortlist included three other projects: the Royale Belge renovation in Brussels, Belgium, by Caruso St John Architects in collaboration with Bovenbouw Architectuur and DDS+; Z33 House for Contemporary Art in Hasselt, Belgium, by Francesca Torzo Architetto; and BRAC University in Dhaka, Bangladesh, by WOHA.

title: Eyes on the Street: Jane Jacobs’ Concept and Contemporary Residential Architecture in Brazil
text:
Eyes on the Street: Jane Jacobs’ Concept and Contemporary Residential Architecture in Brazil

The concept of "eyes on the street" is perhaps the most famous within architectural and urban literature when it comes to urban security. Jane Jacobs uses this expression to refer to people who - consciously or unconsciously - use public spaces or observe them from their homes, generating natural surveillance. A movement that, within our discipline, is encouraged both through quality public spaces and through the powerful relationship between the public and private created through building facades. Advocating for this daily control, Jacobs believes in a way of making architecture and cities that condemns excessive verticalization, reinforced by isolated buildings and single-use ones that deny contact with the street.

title: The Summer Path House / Gieo Architecture
text:
The Summer Path House / Gieo Architecture

The Summer Path is a residential renovation and extension project that transforms the roof of an existing house into a new ground, creating a connection between existing values and a new way of living. Located in a commercial neighborhood in Tho Tang, Phu Tho, Vietnam, the project emerges from a context where the ground level has increasingly been occupied by commercial activities, warehouses, and urban infrastructure.

title: Campbelltown Hospital Redevelopment / Billard Leece Partnership
text:
Campbelltown Hospital Redevelopment / Billard Leece Partnership

Designed by Billard Leece Partnership, the Campbelltown Hospital Stage 2 Redevelopment transforms healthcare delivery for one of Australia's fastest-growing regions through a large-scale, community-focused model of care. Located on Dharawal Country in South West Sydney, the $632 million redevelopment nearly doubles the size of the existing hospital campus, introducing a new 12-storey clinical services building alongside extensive refurbishment works to create an integrated and future-focused health precinct.

title: Critical Regionalism Abroad: Aris Konstantinidis without Greece
text:
Critical Regionalism Abroad: Aris Konstantinidis without Greece

Since the 1980s, critical regionalism has been globally celebrated for imbuing modern architecture with local sensibilities. After rising to international stardom, however, several critical regionalists soon began to erect distinctive albeit “placeless” buildings around the world. This book examines how Aris Konstantinidis (1913–1993), a Greek architect less well known outside his home country, instead propagated his vision of regional modernism to global audiences on his own terms through his publishing and teaching beyond national borders.

title: SALOMON Store MINAMIAOYAMA / kooo architects
text:
SALOMON Store MINAMIAOYAMA / kooo architects

Salomon Store Minami-Aoyama is located in a distinctive space where a narrow alley in Minami- Aoyama extends directly into the semi-basement of the building. For Salomon, a brand that bridges urban lifestyles and outdoor culture, Minami-Aoyama is an ideal location. This iconic Tokyo fashion district sits at the intersection of luxury urbanity and the street culture of Harajuku and Ura-Harajuku. At the same time, the site itself has an unusual quality: the alley seems to flow directly into the building, creating a space that feels slightly external despite being within the city.

title: Shift Pc Suyu Office / RVMN
text:
Shift Pc Suyu Office / RVMN

Emerging in the late 1990s, the Korean PC Bang has served as a social hub within urban youth culture, where friends gather to play games and grab a meal. Going beyond the notion of a simple internet café, it has evolved into a uniquely Korean gaming lounge that combines high-speed internet, high-performance gaming equipment, and an independent F&B service delivered directly to the users' seats.

title: Calm Haven House / ADA Design & Build
text:
Calm Haven House / ADA Design & Build

Calm Haven House was built in 2025. The home belongs to a young couple from the "Land of Coconuts" in the Mekong Delta. They met at university, found a deep connection with each other, and have remained together throughout their journey of dedicating their youth and efforts to the medical profession. As they prepared to welcome their first child, the young doctor couple decided to build their home in the city where they both work. They envisioned a peaceful, tranquil, yet warm and welcoming home—a place where they could relax and recover after the demands of their work.

title: Martha Tavern / CODOO STUDIO
text:
Martha Tavern / CODOO STUDIO

Some bars try to look like homes. With Martha, we decided to do the exact opposite: build a house and open it to the public.

title: House in Belém / Filipe Borges de Macedo
text:
House in Belém / Filipe Borges de Macedo

The dwelling, located in the Casas Económicas das Terras do Forno neighbourhood, inaugurated in 1938 in the parish of Belém, was designed in 1933 by architect Raul Lino. The neighbourhood comprises 204 traditionally designed, low-cost houses intended for civil and military employees, as well as members of the National Trade Unions.

title: Promenade House / studio gm
text:
Promenade House / studio gm

The Promenade House is a residence conceived from the experience of traversing and discovering the landscape. Situated on the shores of a lake and surrounded by an extensive garden, the house does not reveal itself immediately; access occurs along a winding path through the vegetation that gradually leads to the architecture. The path, therefore, is more than mere circulation; it structures the arrival experience, giving rise to the project's name: promenade, in reference to the act of walking and observing.
